themes.consensus_view: Goldman Sachs and Natixis both point to stress in credit tied to AI spending, led by Oracle's default-insurance cost (CDS) sitting near record highs, while other desks only mention AI financing in passing.

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman Sachs and Natixis both flag Oracle's 5-year credit default swap (the cost of insuring against its default) as elevated, and tech as weak in credit.
evidence_quotes: Oracle 5 year cds trades near record 261bps
with Tech clearly underperforming once again

themes.consensus_view: September core CPI came in above forecasts for a second month, and banks point to goods costs (tariffs, diesel and commodities), services and AI-related demand as the pressures, while the Fed is seen as facing a firmer inflation picture than expected.

facts_agreed.claim: September core CPI beat expectations, with the upside spread across goods and services.
evidence_quotes: Core CPI increased by 0.33% in September, above expectations.
The surprise was broadly based for both goods and services

facts_agreed.claim: Goods price gains are being pushed by input costs such as tariffs, commodities and diesel.
evidence_quotes: This reflects pass through of commodities and tariffs
higher diesel costs is taking the baton from tariffs

facts_contested.claim: Whether the core inflation trend is softening or re-accelerating
facts_contested.for_evidence: September CPI Preview: Renewal of a softer trend
facts_contested.against_evidence: The surprise was broadly based for both goods and services

themes.consensus_view: Only Goldman Sachs staked a view, raising its December 2026 Brent forecast because of ongoing oil supply risks, while other desks mention Middle East supply risk without taking a directional stance.

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman Sachs cites ongoing downside risks to oil supply as the reason it raised its year-end Brent forecast.
evidence_quotes: given ongoing downside risks to oil supply

themes.consensus_view: Banks expect the Fed to hike again in December, but they split on whether it hikes on October 28 after the hot September core CPI, with Scotiabank and PNC keeping it live and SEB and Raymond James leaning toward a hold.

facts_agreed.claim: Scotiabank and PNC say the hot September core CPI print keeps an October 28 hike in play, with market odds near 50%.
evidence_quotes: I wouldn't rule out another hike on October 28th
October rate hike odds jumped to just over 50% on the news

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman Sachs and TS Lombard both expect at least one more Fed hike in December.
evidence_quotes: We expect the Fed to deliver one more 25bp hike in December
GIR continues to expect that the Fed will deliver a second hike in December
the probability of a 50BP hike in Dec is not 0

facts_contested.claim: Whether the Fed hikes at the October 27-28 meeting
facts_contested.for_evidence: I wouldn't rule out another hike on October 28th
facts_contested.against_evidence: Several Fed members have said that the Fed can wait before hiking again

facts_contested.claim: Size of the December hike (50bp or 25bp)
facts_contested.for_evidence: the probability of a 50BP hike in Dec is not 0
facts_contested.against_evidence: We expect the Fed to deliver one more 25bp hike in December

themes.consensus_view: Banks mention Chinese hyperscalers mainly as part of the AI spending and earnings story, and only UBS has taken a directional view, saying the risk is skewed to the upside.

facts_agreed.claim: Several desks reference Chinese hyperscalers, their capex cycle and their earnings turn as a live subject without staking a directional view.
evidence_quotes: China tech capex cycle
Chinese hyperscalers earnings inflection
Hyperscaler cloud growth

facts_agreed.claim: UBS sees the balance of risk skewed to the upside for Chinese hyperscalers, with fundamentals holding up better than sentiment implies.
evidence_quotes: we believe the balance of risk as skewed to the upside

themes.consensus_view: Chip and memory stocks have sold off for several days on worries about how the AI buildout gets paid for, while the equipment makers say customer demand still exceeds what they can supply.

facts_agreed.claim: Semiconductor stocks have fallen for several sessions in a row.
evidence_quotes: Semiconductors and memory came under continued pressure, following Monday's fourth straight decline for the SOX
Philly semiconductor index (-0.23%) posting a 5th consecutive decline

facts_agreed.claim: Doubts about financing the AI buildout are weighing on AI-linked stocks.
evidence_quotes: what the credit markets are saying about the ability to continue to finance the AI trade
the AI trade has come under pressure in the repeat funders

facts_agreed.claim: Chip equipment makers report demand above their capacity.
evidence_quotes: not enough to fulfill the customer demand
we cannot meet the demand we have from customers

facts_contested.claim: Whether the chip selloff reflects a weakening upcycle or only a sentiment pullback
facts_contested.for_evidence: we view the duration and strength of the semiconductor upcycle as the more important driver
facts_contested.against_evidence: When one of the generals of the AI trade starts falling, the rest of the army should pay attention.

themes.consensus_view: Banks across eight desks name France's public finances, borrowing costs and 2027 budget as a live concern, but none has staked a directional view yet.

evidence_quotes: France fiscal and debt sustainability
French fiscal sustainability and 2027 election
France government borrowing costs
French 2027 draft budget revenue debate
French 2027 budget fiscal consolidation

themes.consensus_view: Most desks see US stocks as unusually top-heavy and expensive, with a handful of giant companies carrying the index, while one Goldman view argues returns inside the market are better than the narrow headline suggests.

facts_agreed.claim: Banks agree the US equity market is unusually concentrated in a few large stocks and that valuations are stretched.
evidence_quotes: 5 companies carry as much benchmark weight and value as 434 constituents
60% of S&P 500 stocks are down 20% or more from their all-time highs
US equity valuations today are abnormally elevated, sitting well above the Nifty Fifty era

facts_contested.claim: Whether returns beneath the narrow index are healthy or weak
facts_contested.for_evidence: returns within the market are better than many seem to be giving credit for
facts_contested.against_evidence: 60% of S&P 500 stocks are down 20% or more from their all-time highs
